dataset: HLF Pulse — Verified New Zealand Mortgage, Housing & KiwiSaver Reference Dataset
next_expected_update: Monthly (RBNZ / Stats NZ / MBIE Tenancy) & Quarterly (CPI / IRD Student Loans)
about: HLF Pulse is a public reference dataset covering New Zealand mortgage, housing and KiwiSaver statistics. Data is compiled from official releases from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, Stats NZ, Inland Revenue and MBIE Tenancy Services. Where HLF calculates percentages, averages or comparisons from the underlying official data, these are identified as 'Derived by HLF'. HLF does not alter or estimate official statistics. Where source data is unavailable, stale or cannot be verified, the relevant series is excluded.

records.name: Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs investors
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C41
records.source_series_ids: DTINI.MPA (Borrower Gross Income by TDTI band)
records.data_type: HLF-derived borrower-weighted harmonic average (from RBNZ C41 income bands)
records.definition: The borrower-weighted average annual pre-tax gross income reported on approved New Zealand first-home buyer and property investor mortgage applications (combining single and joint applicants).
records.calculation: Borrower-weighted mean across C41 TDTI bands = $144,232 (FHB)
records.formula: Total Gross Income NZDm across all TDTI bands ÷ Implied Borrower Count (Band NZDm ÷ Band Avg Income NZD000s)
records.methodology: Computed from RBNZ Table C41 (Residential mortgage borrower gross income) across all Total Debt-to-Income bands.
records.summary_text: Because mortgage applications often combine two incomes, approved first-home buyers in September 2026 recorded an average gross borrower income of $144.2k nationwide.

records.name: Annual residential construction cost inflation (CPI purchase of newly built home)
records.source_full: Stats NZ — Consumers Price Index (CPI)
records.source_series_ids: Stats NZ CPI Housing & Household Utilities
records.data_type: Officially reported Stats NZ quarterly CPI inflation
records.definition: The annual percentage change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home in New Zealand as measured by the Stats NZ Consumers Price Index (CPI).
records.calculation: Directly reported Stats NZ CPI purchase of new housing = +3.2% YoY
records.formula: Officially reported Stats NZ annual percentage change for purchase of new housing
records.methodology: Published quarterly by Stats NZ within the Consumers Price Index release.
records.summary_text: Residential build-cost inflation has settled into single digits compared with the post-pandemic construction surge—Stats NZ recorded a +3.2% annual change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home in the September 2026 quarter, alongside 3.7% overall CPI inflation.

records.name: First-home buyer high-DTI (>6x) lending share & bank speed-limit headroom
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C40
records.data_type: HLF-derived share & HLF-calculated speed-limit headroom
records.definition: The percentage of new first-home buyer mortgage lending committed at a Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) ratio above 6x gross income, compared against the Reserve Bank's 20% speed-limit allowance.
records.formula: (FHB Lending with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB Lending) × 100; Headroom = 20.0% minus High-DTI Share
records.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C40 (Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income purpose use).
records.summary_text: Most first-home lending currently sits well inside the Reserve Bank's Debt-to-Income limits—in September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer lending had a DTI ratio above 6x, sitting 10.9 percentage points below RBNZ's 20% bank speed-limit allowance.

records.name: Total monthly dollar equity unlocked via mortgage top-ups
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C33
records.data_type: Officially reported dollar volume & HLF-derived average
records.definition: Total monthly dollar lending unlocked by existing New Zealand homeowners through mortgage top-ups on existing properties.
records.formula: Officially reported LVRN.MMB1.AZB dollar total; Avg top-up = LVRN.MMB1.AZB × $1m ÷ LVRN.MMB2.AZB
records.methodology: Sourced from RBNZ Table C33 series LVRN.MMB1.AZB (Top-up lending value) and LVRN.MMB2.AZB (Top-up borrower count).
records.summary_text: Tapping into home equity without selling is one of the most common moves in New Zealand banking—in September 2026, homeowners unlocked $962m in mortgage top-ups across 9,639 existing properties (averaging $100k per top-up).

records.name: First-home buyers approved with a 20% or greater deposit (<=80% LVR)
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
records.data_type: Officially reported count/value & HLF-derived share/average (with market context)
records.definition: The number, percentage share, and average loan size of New Zealand first-home buyers approved with a deposit of 20% or more (LVR <= 80%).
records.formula: (<=80% LVR FHB Borrowers [LVRN.MMB2.CC1] ÷ Total FHB Borrowers [LVRN.MMB2.AC1]) × 100
records.methodology: Sourced from RBNZ Table C31 series for <=80% LVR first-home buyer lending and borrower counts.
records.summary_text: In September 2026, 1,325 first-home buyers (49.7% of first-home approvals, or $680m) were approved with a 20% or greater deposit (≤80% LVR), borrowing an average of $513,208. In practice, a 20% deposit is the standard threshold where banks offer advertised special rates without low-equity margins.

records.name: Annual rolling 12-month first-home buyer mortgage approvals
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
records.data_type: HLF-derived 12-month rolling sum & HLF-calculated comparison
records.definition: The cumulative number and dollar value of first-home buyer mortgages approved across New Zealand over the trailing 12 months, including the number approved with under a 20% deposit.
records.formula: 12-month trailing sum of LVRN.MMB2.AC1 (borrowers), LVRN.MMB1.AC1 (NZDm), and LVRN.MMB2.BC1 (>80% LVR borrowers)
records.methodology: Rolling 12-month sum of monthly RBNZ Table C31 firm commitments to first-home buyers.
records.summary_text: Over the 12 months to September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 33,485 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $19.61B in lending (up from 31,589 loans a year earlier)—including 15,743 buyers (47.0%) who bought with under a 20% deposit.

records.name: First-home buyer share of all bank low-deposit (>80% LVR) lending
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
records.data_type: HLF-derived share (from officially reported RBNZ high-LVR totals)
records.definition: The share of all >80% LVR (under 20% deposit/equity) residential mortgage lending across New Zealand committed to first-home buyers.
records.formula: (FHB >80% LVR Lending [LVRN.MMB1.BC1] ÷ All Borrower >80% LVR Lending [LVRN.MMB1.BA]) × 100
records.methodology: Compares high-LVR first-home commitments against high-LVR commitments across all borrower types combined in RBNZ Table C31.
records.summary_text: First-home buyers account for the majority of bank low-deposit (>80% LVR) mortgage approvals in New Zealand. In September 2026, 67.2% of all low-deposit mortgage dollars ($850m of $1.26B) and 62.0% of low-deposit loans (1,342 of 2,165) were committed to first-home buyers.

records.name: First-home buyer average mortgage size by deposit tier (<20% vs 20%+ deposit)
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
records.data_type: HLF-derived cohort averages & HLF-calculated comparison
records.definition: Comparison of the average approved mortgage size for New Zealand first-home buyers with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR) versus first-home buyers with a 20%+ deposit (<=80% LVR).
records.formula: (LVRN.MMB1.BC1 × $1m ÷ LVRN.MMB2.BC1) minus (LVRN.MMB1.CC1 × $1m ÷ LVRN.MMB2.CC1)
records.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 by dividing total monthly dollar lending in each LVR tier by the number of approved first-home borrowers in that same LVR tier.
records.summary_text: In September 2026, New Zealand first-home buyers approved with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR) borrowed an average of $633,383, compared with $513,208 for buyers with a 20%+ deposit—a $120,175 difference. In practice, higher-income buyers often use low-deposit options to purchase sooner rather than waiting to accumulate a 20% deposit.

records.name: First-home buyers using under 20% deposit
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
records.data_type: HLF-derived share & HLF-calculated comparison (from officially reported RBNZ loan counts & dollar values)
records.definition: First-home buyer mortgage commitments where the Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) exceeds 80% (meaning the buyer has less than a 20% deposit), measured by borrower/loan count alongside officially reported high-LVR dollar lending.
records.formula: (High-LVR FHB Borrowers [LVRN.MMB2.BC1] ÷ Total FHB Borrowers [LVRN.MMB2.AC1]) × 100
records.methodology: Compiled from monthly registered bank returns under RBNZ Table C31. First-home buyers are defined by lending banks as borrowers purchasing a residential property to occupy as a first home.
records.summary_text: Buying a first home without a full 20% deposit is more common than many buyers expect. records.name: Regional KiwiSaver first-home withdrawal averages across New Zealand
records.source_full: Inland Revenue — KiwiSaver Fund Withdrawals by Region
records.source_series_ids: IRD Annual Regional KiwiSaver First-Home Purchase Withdrawals
records.data_type: Officially reported IRD regional totals & HLF-derived per-person / couple averages
records.definition: Average KiwiSaver first-home withdrawal amount per withdrawing member (and two-member couple average) across New Zealand's 16 regions.

records.name: Property investor equity tier breakdown (40%+, 30%–40%, and <30% equity)
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
records.data_type: HLF-derived equity tier distribution (with lender-policy context)
records.definition: Distribution of approved New Zealand residential property investors across three equity tiers: 40%+ equity (<=60% LVR), 30%–40% equity (60% < LVR <= 70%), and under 30% equity (>70% LVR).
records.formula: 40%+ eq = LVRN.MMB2.TN ÷ AN; 30–40% eq = (LVRN.MMB2.FN - DN) ÷ AN; <30% eq = LVRN.MMB2.DN ÷ AN
records.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 investor memo series tracking LVR thresholds at 60% and 70%.
records.summary_text: Many property investors are buying with less than 40% equity. In September 2026, 43.8% of approved NZ property investors had 40%+ equity (≤60% LVR)—while 36.4% bought in the 30%–40% equity band and 19.8% (527 loans, or $337m) were approved with under 30% equity. In practice, lender policy and LVR exemptions determine how much equity an individual investor needs.

records.name: Property investor loans approved with under 20% deposit (>80% LVR) & 20%–30% deposit
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
records.data_type: Officially reported >80% LVR counts/values & HLF-derived 70%–80% LVR tier
records.definition: The number and dollar value of residential property investor mortgages approved with strictly under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR), alongside the 20%–30% deposit tier (70% < LVR <= 80%).
records.formula: >80% LVR = LVRN.MMB2.BN; 70%–80% LVR = LVRN.MMB2.DN minus LVRN.MMB2.BN
records.methodology: In RBNZ Table C31, strictly under-20% deposit investor loans are recorded in >80% LVR (LVRN.MMB2.BN / LVRN.MMB1.BN), while exact 20.0% deposit (80.0% LVR) investor loans sit inside 70% < LVR <= 80% (LVRN.MMB2.DN minus LVRN.MMB2.BN).
records.summary_text: In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 52 investor mortgages ($36m, or 1.9% of investors) with strictly under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR)—up from 34 loans ($23m) a year earlier (and 508 loans / $328m over the past 12 months)—plus another 475 investor loans ($301m, or 17.8%) in the 20%–30% deposit tier (70%–80% LVR). Under RBNZ rules, brand-new builds are exempt from LVR restrictions.

records.name: Property investors approved with under a 30% deposit (>70% LVR)
records.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
records.data_type: Officially reported >70% LVR totals & HLF-derived share (with LVR rule context)
records.definition: The total number, dollar value, and percentage share of New Zealand property investor mortgages approved with under a 30% deposit (>70% LVR).
records.formula: (>70% LVR Investor Borrowers [LVRN.MMB2.DN] ÷ Total Investor Borrowers [LVRN.MMB2.AN]) × 100
records.methodology: Sourced from RBNZ Table C31 Memo Item H2/D2 (Higher than 70% LVR investor borrowers and lending).
records.summary_text: Nearly one in five property investor mortgage approvals in New Zealand is written with less than a 30% deposit. In September 2026, 527 investor loans ($337m, or 19.8% of investor approvals) were approved with under a 30% deposit (>70% LVR)—comprising 475 loans ($301m) in the 20%–30% deposit band and 52 loans ($36m) with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR). Under RBNZ rules, new builds are exempt from LVR restrictions alongside bank speed limits.
